summary:
Our project, AgriShift, is a web-based agricultural support platform designed to help farmers make better decisions about crop selection. As a team, we planned and divided the project into different parts, including frontend development, backend development, data processing, and documentation.

We are developing a system that uses real scientific data from NASA POWER, which provides climate and weather information such as temperature, rainfall, and other environmental conditions. We also use FAO/IIASA GAEZ v5 data to understand crop suitability for different locations. By combining these datasets, our platform aims to provide useful crop recommendations based on local environmental conditions.

Our project addresses the challenge of helping farmers make informed decisions instead of depending only on traditional methods or guesswork. We are using React, Node.js, Express, and MongoDB to build the platform.

We believe AgriShift is important because better crop selection can help reduce farming risks, use resources wisely, and support more sustainable agriculture.
details:
Project Details – AgriShift

Our project, AgriShift, is a web-based platform that helps farmers choose suitable crops according to the climate and environmental conditions of their location.

How Does It Work?

Our platform uses real climate data from NASA POWER, including temperature, rainfall, and other environmental factors. We also use FAO/IIASA GAEZ v5 data to understand which crops are suitable for different areas. By combining these datasets, our system aims to provide farmers with useful crop recommendations based on their local conditions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AgriShift can help farmers make better decisions, reduce the risk of choosing unsuitable crops, and use available resources more effectively. Our main goal is to support smarter farming, improve agricultural planning, and encourage sustainable agriculture, especially in developing countries like Pakistan.

Tools and Technologies

We are developing our platform using:

  • Frontend: React.js
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js
  • Database: MongoDB
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER and FAO/IIASA GAEZ v5
  • Development Tools: VS Code, Git, and GitHub

Creativity and Team Planning

The creative part of our project is bringing NASA's scientific climate data and agricultural datasets together in one easy-to-use platform for farmers. Instead of presenting complex scientific data, we aim to turn it into simple and useful recommendations.

As a team, we considered local farming problems, climate differences between regions, crop suitability, data availability, ease of use, and the needs of farmers. We also divided our responsibilities among team members to work on different parts of the project.

Our vision is to make scientific data useful for everyday farming decisions and help farmers move towards more informed and climate-aware agriculture.
